newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn says worth mulling Telekom stake sale.
newsitem.headline: Bonn says worth mulling Telekom stake sale.

text.p: The German government confirmed on Wednesday that an early sale of part of the state's two-thirds stake in telecommunications giant Deutsche Telekom AG could be on the cards.
"It would be worth considering whether the state should move faster to get rid of its holdings," a spokeswoman for the Finance Ministry in Bonn told Reuters.

She stressed, however, that should the government sell its shares, it would be sure to avoid doing so in a way that could damage either the financial situation of the company or the interests of existing shareholders.

Germany changed its constitution and drafted its Telecommunications Act to allow the privatisation of Telekom, stating the government would not under normal circumstances be allowed to sell its remaining shares until the year 2000.
But the telecoms law does not explicitly rule out an early sale of the government's stake.
Telekom launched Europe's largest ever share listing last November, putting around 25 percent of the company's capital in public hands in a $13 billion initial public offering.
The government still holds the remaining 75 percent.
Telekom shares came under pressure in electronic IBIS trade, and were trading down 90 pfennigs at 38.90 shortly before 0800 GMT.
Some dealers were uncertain whether the government would actually put the shares in the market.
An alternative would be for Bonn to transfer its Telekom holdings to the Kreditanstalt fuer Wiederaufbau, as it did with its remaining Lufthansa shares last year.

In any event, it appears that the government will do all that it can to avoid scaring off nearly two million private investors who took part in the IPO last November by moving shares to market gently.
